author: Rahul kp
title: Book Value
hook: what books say vs what market pays!
simple_words: Book value is what the accounts show. Market value is what buyers will actually pay today.

definitions.meaning: Net worth shown in the balance sheet: total assets less outside liabilities (and preference capital), shared among equity shares.
definitions.note: Per share = equity net worth ÷ equity shares

definitions.meaning: Market price per share multiplied by the number of equity shares outstanding. It is also called market capitalisation.

key_points: ==Book value== comes from accounting records and is based on past cost.
==Market value== reflects what investors expect about future earnings and risk.
The two are rarely equal; a gap shows goodwill, hidden assets or market sentiment.
!!Unlisted companies have no market price!!, so valuation needs other methods.

insight.punchline: Books look back, market looks ahead!
insight.text: Market value above book value means investors expect returns higher than the accounts show.

trick_hook: B for Back, M for Meeting buyers

memory_trick.explanation: Book value looks Back at recorded cost. Market value is where buyers and sellers Meet today and price the future.

steps: Net worth given? Use book value
Share price given? Use market value
Multiply price by shares for market cap
exam_tip: Write the basis in your answer. A valuation without saying book, market or intrinsic basis loses marks.

doubt.question: Can market value be below book value?
doubt.answer: Yes. If investors expect poor earnings, the price falls below net worth per share, so the price-to-book ratio is below 1.

mistakes.wrong: Book value of equity = total assets
mistakes.right: Book value of equity = total assets less outside liabilities (and preference capital, if any).
Market value = market price per share × number of equity shares.

mistakes.wrong: Book value equals market value for a listed company
mistakes.right: The two usually differ, because market price reflects expectations and not only recorded cost.

Checker 1: Key point 1 / table row 2: 'based on past cost' is oversimplified. Under Ind AS, some assets and liabilities are carried at fair value or revalued amounts. Better: 'Book value comes from accounting records, mainly historical cost, as per the accounting policies used.'

Checker 1: Table row 5 (Use, Market Value column): P/B is market price ÷ book value per share, so it uses both values. Better: Market Value column 'Market capitalisation, P/E and market-based (relative) valuation'. P/B can be noted as linking the two.

Checker 1: Definition 1 / mistake 1 right: for net worth (book value of equity), also remove fictitious assets and debit balances of accumulated losses. Better: 'Total assets (excluding fictitious assets) less outside liabilities and preference capital.'
Checker 1: Exam tip: 'loses marks' is stated as a firm rule, which the study material does not lay down. Better: 'Always state the basis (book, market or intrinsic) clearly in your answer.'
